faq.q: Can you live with one kidney?
faq.a: Yes. Many people are born with one kidney or donate one, and a single healthy kidney can do the work of filtering the blood.

faq.q: How much spare capacity do kidneys have?
faq.a: A lot. The two kidneys together can filter much more than the body needs at rest, so the body can cope even when kidney function drops a fair way.
asks: Tell me about the big spare capacity

faq.q: What happens when someone has only one kidney?
faq.a: The remaining kidney enlarges and each of its filtering units works harder, so overall filtering rises towards what two kidneys did.
asks: Tell me about how one can grow

faq.a: The kidneys sit at the back of the belly, one on each side of the spine, just below the ribs, which help protect them.

faq.q: Why are some organs single and others paired?
faq.a: It depends on how each organ forms in the developing body. Organs that grow from both sides, like kidneys and lungs, are paired, while ones that form in the middle, like the heart and liver, are single.
asks: Why do we have one heart but two lungs?

facts: Kidneys are about the size of a fist, around 10 to 12 centimetres long.
After one kidney is removed, the remaining kidney typically enlarges and increases its filtering.
